text:
maya: Heads up — drift-watcher just flagged a reconciliation failure between prod and staging for network-related resources. It looks like a cache checksum mismatch is causing GitOps to skip apply. Anyone on call?

Drift-watcher: Automated alert: 
- scope: cluster/redwood-prod vs repo/main
- resources: Service(frontend-lb), NetworkPolicy/allow-infra, ConfigMap/gitops-cache
- error: cache checksum mismatch: expected=0x7a1c got=0x2f9b
- reconcile status: queued -> failed (automerge skipped)

raj: I'm on it. Quick question: does this look like the same heuristic-change we saw after the cache refactor last week?

linh: yea — our cache serializer now drops ordering of annotations which changes hash. GitOps operator uses the raw checksum in the cache to short-circuit reconciliation. If the checksum is different but the normalized object is identical, operator incorrectly assumes drift.

sara: ugly. Can we safely force a reconcile for the affected namespaces without mass rollout?

maya: prefer a narrow fix: 1) unblock prod (one-off reconcile) 2) update parity checker to normalize before hashing 3) patch operator to compare normalized checksums in next rollout.

raj: doing 1) now. Running a one-off forced apply for the three resources in prod namespace:
```bash
# refresh gitops cache for affected cluster
kubectl -n gitops exec deploy/gitops-operator -- /bin/gitopsctl refresh --cluster redwood-prod --resources frontend-lb,allow-infra,gitops-cache
# fallback: remove stale configmap key so operator recomputes
kubectl -n gitops delete configmap gitops-cache --ignore-not-found
```

ops-bot: Deploy bot: started reconcile job job/reconcile-1987654321 (uid: fb3a9)

raj: reconcile job completed for Service(frontend-lb) and NetworkPolicy/allow-infra, still failing for ConfigMap/gitops-cache because operator immediately re-wrote the old checksum. Going to delete and let operator recreate.

linh: for 2) parity-checker patch: normalization rules we want to apply before hashing: sort annotations, strip transient annotations (kubectl.kubernetes.io/*, last-applied-configuration), normalize boolean strings. Example normalization pipeline:
```bash
kubectl get cm gitops-cache -n gitops -o json \
  | jq 'del(.metadata.annotations."kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration") | .metadata.annotations |= (to_entries|sort_by(.key)|from_entries)' \
  | sha256sum
```
This makes hashes stable across serializer changes. I'll open a PR to the parity-checker and add unit tests.

sara: For safety on prod, can we run the parity-checker in dry-run against prod after the one-off reconcile? Want to see what else would have flipped.

maya: yes — run dry-run and post output here before merging. Also let's add a temporary guard to the operator to fallback to full diff if checksum mismatches and dry-run=false.

linh: ack. I'll add a feature flag `operator.normalizeChecksums=true` behind a rollout. Plan: patch parity-checker PR -> add integration test -> enable flag on staging -> roll to prod.

raj: update: deleted gitops-cache configmap, operator recreated it and reconcile completed. No user-facing impact observed.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: reconcile job job/reconcile-1987654321 completed successfully (runtime 34s) :thumbsup:

maya: thanks. Next actions:
- linh: open PR for normalization and operator guard (assign to raj for review)
- raj: run parity-checker dry-run across prod and staging and paste results
- sara: prepare rollback note and change window in case parity patch causes surprises

sara: tagging on-call infra lead for visibility @raj :eyes:

raj: will post dry-run results in ~15m.

maya: nice work team. Recommend we log this as an infra incident with severity P3 so we track the parity fix and add to weekly on-call runbook. :spiral_note_pad:
